correctness.rationale: Read actual RESULT.md and verify_spiral.py. Composition diagonalizes on the given orthonormal monomials with eigenvalues (ae^{iθ})^n; its numerical range is their attainable probability barycenters. Let k=floor(π/θ), t={π/θ}. The most negative imaginary eigenvalue M=a^k max_{j≥1}a^j sin((j−t)θ), yielding upper bound rho≤M, uniformly M/(θa^k)=H_a(t)+O_a(θ²) by sin remainder and exponentially bounded j³a^j. A triangle of actual eigenvalues at indices 0, floor(π/(2θ)), and k+j* contains zero; stable edge-distance inequalities yield rho≥M/(1+a^k). The middle vertex ratio dominates θa^k since a^(p-k)/θ→∞. A finite j* bound follows from j a^j decay. Thus rho=θa^(π/θ)(a^(−t)H_a(t)+O_a(θ²+a^(π/θ))), uniform t; discrete differences give ceil-maximizer and period seam; the triangle absorbs the eigenvalue tail to prove closed finite polygonality for sufficiently small θ. Independent stable-trigonometric checks covered a=1/2,3/4 small θ, not continuum proof.
